processes.name: Real-time position and schedule instructions to trading group for Enpower/CAPS entry
processes.description: The West Hourly desk manager emails the real-time group each time the desk is short, long, or must carry losses or congestion, giving MW, hours, price and which book to use. Traders then key the buys, sales and schedules into Enpower and CAPS by hand, and corrections follow as extra emails.
processes.stall_points: Instructions are sent piecemeal (the same short notice was re-forwarded three times as more APX purchases were made) and rely on each trader keying deals into the correct book. Missing deals are found afterwards.
processes.automation: Generate the deal tickets in Enpower/CAPS directly from a structured position sheet instead of free-text emails. Validate book, counterparty and hours on entry.

processes.name: Prior month adjustment (PMA) and settlement dispute chasing
processes.description: The desk manager reviews month-end PMA sheets, finds revenue or cost mismatches against Enpower, and emails Settlements to explain or correct them. Disputes and annuity corrections go back and forth over days, with Settlements chasing Houston for the other side of a deal.
processes.stall_points: The offsetting side of a deal is missing from Settlements' processes. The $108,000 WBOM PMA stayed open across several emails, and the only fallback is pulling tapes.
processes.automation: Auto-match PMA lines to Enpower deal changes and flag one-sided adjustments (e.g. revenue reversed with no cost reversed) before the sheet reaches the desk.

evidence.quote: Why does a change in counterparty result in a loss of revenue?

ST-Whourly will pay LT-NW our average hourly price per mw for that energy.

processes.name: Daily SAR/INC reconciliation and EPE reconciliation sheet
processes.description: After the DPR arrives, the desk runs a SAR against the INC sheet and the CAPS/Enpower position to find variances, then zeroes duplicate deals or logs variances. A shared EPE reconciliation sheet has to be completed every day, even when there are no variances.
processes.stall_points: Real-time cuts are not in CAPS, so the SAR and INC only match once the manager adds them by hand. The shift skipped the EPE sheet, and Houston treats a blank sheet as if the CARP was not run.
processes.automation: Run the SAR, INC and CARP comparison automatically each morning and write the reconciliation sheet, including a 'no variance' entry. List unexplained deltas for review.

evidence.quote: Even if there are no variances, please complete the July EPE Reconciliation sheet going forward.
Houston will assume that no one ran the CARP if the sheet has no entries.
The SAR and INC sheet are matching if the 42 mw purchase from the imbalance at $44 is factored in
We had some double deal-entry last night under the ST-WBOM book.
we show no variances between the Real Time El Paso model and our CARP report.

processes.name: Forwarding CAISO/FERC market notices and rule changes to the real-time group
processes.description: The desk manager forwards CAISO notices, price-cap clarifications, outage protocols and transmission tips to the real-time group or individual traders. He adds interpretation and asks people to read and apply them. Each notice is re-forwarded by hand to different lists.
processes.stall_points: The same notice is forwarded separately to several people (the judge's summary and the FAQ went to Kate and Ryan separately). Rules change repeatedly, such as the cap and the new OASIS site, and each change needs a new broadcast.
processes.automation: Route CAISO market notices to a shared distribution list with an auto-summary and an acknowledgement tracker, instead of manual forwards.

processes.name: Gas deal entry, extension and release requests in Sitara/Unify (Houston logistics)
processes.description: Schedulers and settlements staff email Daren Farmer or Houston Pipe Line contacts to add deals, extend terms, release deals or fix pricing in Sitara and Unify. Requests move through several intermediaries before someone with the right access acts.
processes.stall_points: Requesters do not know who owns the deal or system access, so mails bounce between people (the same ask is repeated after no answer). A deal sits unreleased in Sitara and the invoice waits.
processes.automation: Provide a single deal-change request queue that routes to the owner with the deal, meter and volume fields pre-filled. Show status so requesters need not chase.

processes.name: Daily EES model/sheet distribution and MPC reconciliation
processes.description: A daily EES model or sheet is emailed to a short list. Kate Symes reports that the settlements people who need it still do not receive it. Month-end MPC numbers are reworked from last year's inc and service sheets under time pressure.
processes.stall_points: The sheet goes to the wrong recipients, so the group that needs it never receives it. MPC numbers are dug out of old sheets by hand.
processes.automation: Send the daily file to a standing settlements distribution list automatically. Keep inc and service sheets in a lookup so MPC figures can be pulled directly.

processes.name: Misdirected mail to Bill Williams III and address book corrections
processes.description: Colleagues repeatedly send project and trading mail to Bill Williams III instead of Bill Williams. He forwards each one to the right person and asks the sender to fix the address book.
processes.stall_points: Senders keep choosing the wrong contact, so each message is forwarded and explained again.
processes.automation: Add a directory alias or auto-reply for the near-duplicate name so the mail reaches the right person.
